item.title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
item.description:
A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
Xiujuan He, Jiyong Eom, Sha Yu, Shu Liu, Wenru Xu, and Yuyu Zhou
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7417–7454, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7417-2026, 2026
Buildings use large amounts of energy for heating and cooling. Cutting carbon emissions requires accurate forecasts of that demand, which depends on knowing the outdoor temperature at which buildings switch on heating or cooling. We combined energy use records with climate information and applied machine learning to create the first global dataset of these thresholds across many regions. It improves energy demand predictions by about 10 %, supporting smarter energy planning and climate policy.

item.title: Ground-motion dataset for shallow earthquakes in Colombia
item.description:
Ground-motion dataset for shallow earthquakes in Colombia
Daniel Martinez-Jaramillo, Sreeram-Reddy Kotha, F. Ramón Zúñiga, and Pierre Lacan
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7403–7415, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7403-2026, 2026
Colombia is regularly struck by damaging earthquakes. We gathered and uniformly processed 7550 recordings from 667 shallow earthquakes into a single open collection describing each earthquake, recording site and level of shaking. Comparison with widely used prediction methods confirmed its quality. The collection can help engineers design safer buildings and improve earthquake hazard maps in Colombia and similar regions.

item.title: A global petrophysical database for igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks
item.description:
A global petrophysical database for igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks
Heather Anne Sheldon, David N. Dewhurst, Elise Bekele, Matthias Raiber, Dirk Mallants, Chris Turnadge, and Gareth Williams
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-556,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created a global database of rock property measurements to facilitate modelling and decision making across a range of geoscientific fields. The Global Petrophysical Database incorporates more than 112,000 measurements from over 600 publications, including both in-situ and laboratory measurements, along with associated metadata (e.g. rock type, location, depth). This comprehensive resource will save researchers time in identifying rock property values for their investigations.

item.title: An African Tree Crown–Stem Allometry Dataset for Monitoring Trees Outside Forests and Landscape Restoration
item.description:
An African Tree Crown–Stem Allometry Dataset for Monitoring Trees Outside Forests and Landscape Restoration
Tabitha Alimo, David Skole, Jay Samek, Dan Ndalowa, Vincent Oeba, Judith Kamoto, Alfred Chioza, Chad Papa, Justine Spore, Darby Levin, John Brandt, and Tangu Tumeo
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-756,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We measured 3,493 trees across Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, and Malawi to solve a key problem: satellites can see tree crowns but not trunks, which are needed to estimate biomass and carbon. We found strong links between crown size and trunk diameter, although relationships varied among landscapes. By linking field measurements with very high-resolution satellite imagery, this dataset enables more accurate, large-area monitoring of scattered trees, restoration progress, and carbon storage.
